summary: Perf critic, acceptance r1. Every test used the real game at 1920x1080 on this M1 Max: shots/accept/r1-perf/*.mjs, with screenshots in shots/accept/r1-perf/. Other agents' browsers were running at the same time (load average 7-23), so contention-sensitive real-time numbers were re-measured once the machine was quieter. GPU cost was measured with __br.fx.bench, which is GPU-synchronised and takes the best of 3 runs. THE GOOD. At 1080p dpr 1 there is a lot of headroom. One frame costs 2.2-4.3 ms of GPU and 2.5-5 ms of CPU (three.js is about 3 ms of that). On a quiet machine the city held a steady 119.6 fps, with p95 10.0 ms and p99 10.3 ms (headless Chromium is capped at 120 Hz). Full real-time autopilot races ran on every track, to results, with 0 console errors and 0 stub fallbacks. Draw budget at high quality: max 252 / 291 / 289 calls (coast / city / mountain) and max 1.01 M / 1.19 M / 1.01 M triangles. Medium: 236-292 calls, ≤1.14 M triangles. Low: 166-223 calls, ≤0.71 M triangles. All 9 quality x track combinations booted and raced with no errors. Memory is stable. Over 4 full races, 3 restarts and 7 quick cycles, the GPU objects return to 18-22 geometries, 12 textures and 36 programs at every menu. The JS heap at the menu stays flat after GC (34.1 → 34.7 MB over 6 cycles). Bus handlers (112), window listeners (31) and DOM nodes (356) do not leak. WebGL context loss followed by restore recovers in about 200 ms and keeps rendering. KO, chain, WRECKED and SHOWTIME cinematics hold about 119 fps. The finish → results transition has no long tasks. Menu screens run at 120 fps. THE BAD: hitches. (1) Every cold race start freezes the intro flyover for 0.5-1.4 s, because 50-57 shader programs compile synchronously in the first race frame and nothing precompiles. Every restart recompiles 25-32 programs (0.2-0.8 s). (2) The first respawn or ghost fade in every race compiles 5-8 programs mid-race. That costs 29-51 ms on a quiet machine and up to 753 ms under load. Rider extras, KO crash variants, particles at GO and world props that come out of the fog cull add more first-use compiles. (3) Robustness hole: save values and URL params are not validated. An outdated bike id in the save blocks every race start. An unknown quality value boots with fx on its stub and every bike replaced by the fallback. A polished racer has no shader hitches and survives a stale save, so this is a fail (6/10) despite the strong frame rate.

issues.title: Race start and restart freeze the intro for 0.2-1.4 s (all shaders compile in the first race frame)
issues.detail: Setup: fresh page per track, menu → __br.start(), high quality, real time, quiet machine (shots/accept/r1-perf/cold-start.mjs). The first intro frames take: coast 475 ms; city 782 ms and then 602 ms; mountain 467 ms and then 259 ms. In that first race frame, 50 / 57 / 56 programs compile synchronously (frame CPU 266 / 358 / 252 ms). A CPU profile of a mountain start shows 1.24 s in three.js program setup, 0.76 s native '(program)' time and 211 ms in getProgramInfoLog. renderer.debug.checkShaderErrors is left on, and nothing in src calls compile or compileAsync. Restart (flow:restartRace, used by pause 重新开始 and results 再来一局) recompiles 25-32 programs every time: compile frames of 127-189 ms, gaps of coast 208 ms, city 560 + 283 ms, mountain 218 + 150 ms. This happens because endSession() disposes the old track first (live programs drop from 77 to 36) before the new session renders.
issues.fix: In game.startRace, after RaceSession.create and the attaches but before show('race'), run a warm-up step. fx exposes a warm(scene, camera) hook that binds its HalfFloat MSAA scene target, and core awaits renderer.compileAsync(app.scene, app.camera, app.scene) (non-blocking with KHR_parallel_shader_compile) with LOD-hidden objects temporarily visible. Then render one hidden frame so the texture uploads happen behind the loading screen (hold it at 90-98 %). Set renderer.debug.checkShaderErrors = import.meta.env.DEV. For restarts, build the new session before disposing the old one, or keep track materials cached per track and quality, so the cached programs survive.

issues.title: First rider fade, rider extras and KO crash variants compile shaders mid-race (29-51 ms quiet, up to 753 ms under load)
issues.detail: RiderFade (src/actors/fade.ts) creates its transparent and depth clone materials on first use: respawn materialise, invulnerability pulse, pigeon ghost. The first fade of every race compiles 5-8 programs in one frame: actors:rider fade, bikes:body, bikes:hull and bikes:depth variants. On a quiet machine (fade.mjs) that frame takes coast 29 ms, city 31 ms, mountain 51 ms; the pigeon ghost at city s≈525 took 47.5 ms (who.mjs). Under machine load: coast low s≈450 produced one 753 ms frame, city medium 301 ms, mountain high 95 ms and 108 ms. Rider extras add more first-use compiles: a Sprite inside rider:shiba (s≈187) and a MeshBasicMaterial mesh under rider:pelican (s≈196). The first KOs compile crash variants (skinned bike:body toon and hull, depth, debris Mesh and Sprite) at 25-33 ms each (ko.mjs). Every race hits at least the fade compile.
issues.fix: Build the fade clones once per template material, shared by every rider that uses that material, at view creation. Warm every variant during the intro: on the first intro frame, call fade.set(0.99) on each view and show the steam and glint sprites at opacity 0 for one rendered frame, then restore. Do the same for the crash-time variants. Acceptance check: renderer.info.programs does not grow after the GO frame.

issues.title: Save values and URL params are not validated: a stale bike id blocks every race, an unknown quality disables fx
issues.detail: SaveStore.load() (src/core/save.ts) shallow-merges whatever is in localStorage. If the save holds a bike id that no longer exists (for example {"bike":"rocket"} after a bike is renamed), every race start fails with '[game] could not start race … reading durability' (core/rider.ts:11) and drops back to the menu. This repeats on every attempt until the player wipes the save. A save or ?quality= value that is not a known quality ('ultra', 'potato') makes PostPipeline's PRESETS[quality] undefined. The game then boots with fx on its stub (no post, no particles, no KO cinematic) and replaces every bike with the fallback bike (8 x '[actors] createBike … failed'). ?race=nowhere races on the stub world, and the loading screen throws in calendarFor. Repro: shots/accept/r1-perf/badsave.mjs and badparams.mjs.
issues.fix: Validate field by field in SaveStore.load(): quality must be low, medium or high; bike and owned bikes must be BIKES keys, otherwise fall back to the default; numbers must be finite and clamped; booleans must be booleans. In game.ts, validate ?quality and ?race against the known lists before use. Add a node test that loads corrupt and outdated saves.

issues.title: Particle programs compile in the GO frame, right when the launch boost is timed
issues.detail: fx.particles.solid and fx.particles.add compile in the GO frame on every track and quality: 19 ms quiet (city), 63 ms on mountain high, 65 ms on coast low, 94 ms on city at dpr 2. That is the exact moment the player is holding throttle for the launch boost.
issues.fix: In fx.attach(session), warm both pool programs during the intro: emit one invisible particle per pool, or compile the pool meshes with the fx target bound, so the GO burst draws with programs that are already linked.

issues.title: World props hidden by the fog cull at the grid compile when they first appear mid-race
issues.detail: Objects that world/lod.ts hides at the start are skipped by the first render, so their programs compile when they first become visible: mountain turbineRotors (a 170 ms frame under load) and gondolas (51 ms) at s≈1474-1600; city:walls (36 ms, s≈1491); city:riverGlow, city:vaultMirror and an unnamed Mesh<track:city> (10-92 ms, s≈492-1605); coast tunnelShade, the boats hull and an unnamed Mesh<track:coast> (7-14 ms). Source: lifecycle.mjs and who.mjs program logs.
issues.fix: At the end of createTrack, after installFogCull: temporarily make every LOD-hidden object visible, compile once with a HalfFloat render target bound (so the output key matches fx), then restore. Alternatively, publish the list so the core warm-up from issue 1 can include it.

issues.title: Riders are never frustum-culled and have no distance LOD
issues.detail: instantiate() sets frustumCulled = false on every skinned body and its hull. With all 7 rivals moved 400 m behind the camera, they still cost 21 draw calls and 163k triangles per frame (bodies, hulls and the shadow pass), about 17 % of the frame's triangles for meshes nobody can see. At any distance the 8 riders cost 46-53 calls and 300-357k triangles, about 35 % of the frame (breakdown.mjs).
issues.fix: Give each body a bounding sphere padded to the rig's reach (or refresh it from the root bone) and turn frustum culling back on. Beyond about 50 m, drop castShadow and the hull; optionally swap in a coarser SDF mesh for far riders.

issues.title: High quality renders at native Retina resolution with a wasted MSAA backbuffer and no render scale
issues.detail: game.ts sets pixelRatio = min(devicePixelRatio, 2) for high and antialias: quality !== 'low' on the main canvas. All 3D renders into fx's own MSAA HalfFloat target, and the canvas only receives the composite quad, so the MSAA backbuffer is pure memory and resolve cost (about 66 MB at 1080p, about 265 MB at 4K including depth). At dpr 2 the GPU frame grows about 5x: city 2.2 ms at 1080p vs 8.9-10.8 ms at 3840x2160, of which post is about 4 ms. In real time, the 4K city averaged 72 fps with p95 18.6 ms, so at least 5 % of frames run below 60 fps (56 fps under heavy load). A MacBook-sized 1512x982 viewport at dpr 2 averaged 78 fps with p95 17.8 ms. There is no render-scale setting or dynamic resolution to absorb this.
issues.fix: Use antialias: false for the main renderer. Cap the high-quality drawing buffer at about 1440p-equivalent pixels, or add a 渲染比例 setting. Add a dynamic-resolution governor driven by the frame-time EMA (pixel ratio 0.7-1.0 of the cap). Ask fx to compute bloom from a half-resolution copy.

issues.title: City dressing blocks the loading screen for about 0.65 s in one task
issues.detail: The city dressing stage runs as one synchronous block of about 730 ms (neon, streets, 200 pedestrians, fill blocks). It produces long tasks of 646 ms on a cold start and 503 ms on restart (cold-start.mjs), which freeze the loading bar and runner. Mountain shows the same pattern at a smaller size: 245 ms on a quiet machine, 581 ms under load, with 'leg blend' taking 342 ms in env/mountain-legs.ts.
issues.fix: Split the dressing into sub-steps (neon, streets, life, fill, P5 boards) and await a yield (world/breathe) between them, so that no task runs longer than about 100 ms. env-mountain should do the same for leg blending and terrain grading.

issues.title: Loading runner is JS-driven and animates 'left', so it freezes on every long task
issues.detail: loading.ts moves the runner icon with rider.style.left and the bar with scaleX, from ui.update on every frame. Both stop dead during every build long task (issue 8, and the 0.5-1.4 s start freeze in issue 1), and writing 'left' forces a layout every frame.
issues.fix: Drive the runner with transform: translateX(...) plus a CSS keyframe run cycle, so it keeps moving on the compositor while the main thread is busy. Use JS only to set the target progress.

issues.title: __br.sim.riders debug closure keeps the previous RaceSession alive at the menu
issues.detail: A heap snapshot taken after quitting to the menu shows the retainer path Window.__br.sim.riders (closure) → Context.session → RaceSession. The whole previous race stays reachable: 1100 Object3D, 487 BufferGeometry and 132 materials, about 3-10 MB of JS heap. After that hook is replaced, no RaceSession is live. The leak does not accumulate (the next race replaces it) and the GPU side is already disposed (retainer.mjs).
issues.fix: In sim/physics.ts, create the debug closures outside the scope that captures the session: read the riders from a holder object that dispose() sets to null, or assign a module-level function that returns an empty list.
